title: Webhook retry storm + TLS session eviction caused upstream runtime restarts and widespread 5xx
text:
Webhook retry storm + TLS session eviction caused upstream runtime restarts and widespread 5xx

description:
Issue summary:
Customer Papertrail Labs reported a sudden rise in 5xx responses beginning 2026-03-10 14:07 UTC affecting short-lived streaming and small-embedding requests. Error pattern showed API Gateway returning 502/503/504 with rapid retries from the customer's webhook integration.

Impact:
- Multiple customers in us-west-2 experienced elevated 5xx rates (~8-12% error rate for affected routes) for ~45 minutes.
- Live chat and embedding endpoints for Papertrail Labs degraded; some streaming sessions dropped mid-response.
- Some requests returned large latency spikes before failing, increasing token cost for customers.

Environment:
- prod | us-west-2
- Redwood hosted API (edge -> api-gateway -> edge-proxy -> serving-runtime)
- Keystore hot-rotate job scheduled 2026-03-10 14:02 UTC

Observable symptoms:
- Rapid sequence of inbound webhook retries from Papertrail Labs (multiple downstream services) beginning 14:05 UTC.
- TLS session cache on edge-proxy shows eviction churn correlated with keystore rotation logs.
- Upstream serving-runtime processes restarted (OOM-like exits) around 14:09–14:12 UTC, causing API gateway to surface 502/503.

Requested customer-visible fields:
- First byte times and error traces for affected requests
- Confirmation of rollback/mitigation and long-term fix

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Trigger repeated webhook delivery retries to the same tenant route at ~100–200 rps for ~2 minutes.
2) Simulate keystore rotation on the edge-proxy (hot reload of TLS keys).
3) Observe elevated TLS handshake times, session eviction, and upstream connection resets leading to 5xx from api-gateway.

Attachments: logs and Grafana dashboards linked below.

investigation_notes:
14:12 UTC: Triage — correlated keystore rotation window with TLS session eviction counters on edge-proxy (tls.session.evictions increased x6)
Hypothesis A: TLS session eviction during hot-rotate caused handshake latency; api-gateway hedged retries amplified load to serving-runtime leading to ephemeral worker exhaustion.
Hypothesis B: Incoming webhook retry pattern concentrated connections to a small subset of worker shards, causing local accept-queue saturation and evictions.
SRE action: Scoped to us-west-2 and throttled the customer webhook traffic via per-tenant token bucket at 14:18 UTC to arrest the retry storm.
Observation: After throttling retries and temporarily pausing keystore hot-rotate, 5xx rate returned to baseline by 14:52 UTC. Runtime restarts stopped and keepalive FD usage stabilized.

comments:
Support (Aisha): We've opened this incident after Papertrail reported repeated 502/503s starting ~14:07 UTC. Collecting traces and asking for customer request IDs.
Papertrail (Customer Contact - Jordan Lee): We retried deliveries when our endpoint responded 5xx. We see many TLS handshake errors on our side too. Happy to pause retries if you need us to.
SRE (Ben): Temporarily throttled inbound webhook retries for Papertrail at 14:18 UTC and paused keystore reload; monitoring for recovery.
Eng (Rosa): Investigating runtime restart stack traces — initial signs point to sudden connection churn on single shard causing main loop SIGABRT due to assert in proxy loop; collecting core dumps.
Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed pause of upstream webhook retries at 14:20 UTC; we saw error rate fall starting 14:34 UTC.
SRE (Ben): Post-recovery, deployed a soft-fix at 14:50 UTC that adds a small accept-queue buffer and defers TLS session pruning during keystore rotations in us-west-2.
Customer (Jordan): Issue resolved for us. Appreciate the quick mitigation and the suggested follow-ups.

resolution:
Mitigation performed: 1) Throttled the offending tenant's webhook retry traffic at the API gateway (per-tenant token-bucket) to prevent retry amplification. 2) Paused keystore hot-rotate while the eviction thresholds stabilized. 3) Deployed temporary soft-fix to edge-proxy to avoid aggressive TLS session pruning during hot-rotate and added 5s jitter to accept-queue backoff. 4) Patched serving-runtime to make accept-queue handling more resilient to concentrated conn storms (PR merged: runtime#4821).

Root cause: Combined failure mode — customer-side retry amplification concentrated traffic on a narrow shard + keystore hot-rotate triggered TLS session evictions. The eviction churn increased handshake latency and connection resets; api-gateway hedged retries amplified the pressure into serving-runtime causing worker crashes.

Follow-ups assigned:
- SRE: implement safer keystore rotation (conservative session pruning) and add canary rollout for future rotations (owner: Ben Rodriguez).
- Runtime team: harden proxy loop to survive transient reset waves and add better shard-level load distribution (owner: Rosa Martinez).
- Support/Customer Success: advise Papertrail on exponential backoff and jitter on webhook retries; share recommended retry policy (owner: Aisha Kumar).

Status: Resolved 2026-03-12 after deploy and customer confirmation. Postmortem scheduled on confluence page linked above.

action_items:
SRE to ship keystore rotation guard (avoid session prune > 20% during hot-rotate) — due 2026-03-24
Runtime to add shard smoothing for tenant-heavy routes — due 2026-04-07
CS to send webhook-retry best-practice note to Papertrail Labs and update developer docs — due 2026-03-18
